definition_zh: 社会流动；社会地位的升降（社会学概念，指个人或群体在不同社会位置之间的移动）
definition_en: the movement of individuals or groups between social positions, classes or strata
core_image: 一架透明的阶梯，每一格站着不同职业的人，有人向上跨两级，有人向下滑一级
scene: 城市旧公寓的楼下住着清洁工，楼上刚搬来一户医生家庭。Social mobility is measured by comparing the occupations of parents and their grown children.
sceneCN: 这里 social mobility 指「个人或群体在不同社会阶层之间的位置变动」（第 1 个义项：社会位置的上升或下降）；句意为社会流动通过比较父母与成年子女的职业来衡量。图中可辨识物件：透明阶梯、不同职业的剪影、上下箭头、普查表格。

pos.zh: 社会流动；社会地位变动（不可数名词短语）

forms.label: 不可数用法
forms.form: social mobility（指过程或总体状况时不加 -s）

derivatives.zh: 可移动的 / 移动电话
在社会方面；在社会地位上

senses.title: Rise or fall in social position
senses.titleCN: 社会位置的上升或下降
senses.definition: movement of an individual or group from one social rank or class to another
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体从一个社会等级或阶层移动到另一个
senses.example: Social mobility is measured by comparing the occupations of parents and their grown children.
senses.exampleCN: 社会流动通过比较父母与成年子女的职业来衡量。
senses.why: mobility comes from a Latin word for being movable, so the phrase treats rank as a position one can move out of.
senses.whyCN: mobility 源自拉丁语中「可移动」的说法，因此这个短语把等级看作可以离开的位置。

senses.title: Upward mobility
senses.definition: movement to a higher class, income bracket or status than the starting point
senses.definitionCN: 移动到比起始点更高的阶层、收入档位或地位
senses.example: A scholarship carried her from a factory floor to a law office, a classic case of upward mobility.
senses.exampleCN: 一份奖学金把她从工厂车间送进律师事务所，这是向上流动的典型例子。
senses.why: the direction is supplied by upward, not by mobility itself; the noun only says that movement happened.
senses.whyCN: 方向由后加的「向上」说明，这个词本身只表示发生了移动。

senses.title: Downward mobility
senses.definition: movement to a lower class or status than the one a person started from
senses.definitionCN: 移动到比原本起点更低的阶层或地位
senses.example: Plant closures sent many skilled workers into downward mobility.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭使许多熟练工人陷入向下流动。
senses.why: the same noun covers loss of position, because motion by itself has no direction.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也能表示地位失落，因为移动本身并无方向。

senses.title: Intergenerational mobility
senses.definition: a change in status between parents and their children
senses.definitionCN: 父母与子女之间社会地位的变化
senses.example: Intergenerational mobility is lower where schooling depends on family income.
senses.exampleCN: 在求学依赖家庭收入的地区，代际流动更低。
senses.why: inter- means between, so the comparison runs across generations rather than inside one life.
senses.whyCN: 前缀意为「之间」，所以比较跨过世代，而不是在一个人一生之内进行。

senses.title: Intragenerational mobility
senses.definition: a change in a person's own status over a working life
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在自己一生工作年限内的地位变化
senses.example: Intragenerational mobility shows up as promotions, layoffs and career switches.
senses.exampleCN: 代内流动表现为晋升、裁员与转行。
senses.why: intra- means within, so the comparison stays inside a single lifetime.
senses.whyCN: 前缀意为「内部」，所以比较保持在一个人一生之内。

senses.title: Occupational mobility
senses.definition: movement between jobs, trades or employers
senses.definitionCN: 在工作、行业或雇主之间的移动
senses.example: Occupational mobility rose as whole trades disappeared and new ones appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 随着整批行业消失、新行业出现，职业流动上升了。
senses.why: occupation names the channel through which social position usually changes.
senses.whyCN: 职业是标示社会位置变化最常用的通道。

senses.title: Structural mobility
senses.definition: movement produced by a change in the shape of the economy rather than by individual effort
senses.definitionCN: 由经济结构变化而非个人努力带来的地位移动
senses.example: The shift from farms to factories produced structural mobility on a huge scale.
senses.exampleCN: 从农场到工厂的转变带来了大规模的结构流动。
senses.why: when the number of professional jobs grows, people move up together without anyone else moving down.
senses.whyCN: 当专业职位总量增长时，人们会一起上移，并不需要别人下移来腾位。

senses.title: Measured rates of movement
senses.definition: the statistical rate at which people change class or occupation in a society
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会中人们改变阶层或职业的统计比率
senses.example: Researchers compare mobility rates across countries using census records.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者用普查记录比较各国的流动率。
senses.why: a social fact becomes researchable once it is counted as a rate per generation.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把社会事实按世代折算成比率，它就变得可以研究。

intro.en: Social goes back through socialis to Latin socius 'companion, ally'; mobility goes back through mobilis and mobilitas to movere 'to move'. The two words were joined as a technical phrase in modern sociology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: social 经 socialis 上溯到拉丁 socius「同伴、盟友」；mobility 经 mobilis、mobilitas 上溯到 movere「移动」。两词在近代社会学中固定连用成术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally, partner'. Its deeper origin is not settled, and any Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than attested evidence.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友、伙伴」。其更深来源尚无定论，凡为其提出的印欧形式均属重构，而非有据可查的材料。

items.en: The adjective socialis described what belongs to allies or to companionship, and it passed through French into English as social, naming relations between people.
items.cn: 形容词 socialis 指属于盟友或同伴关系的，经法语进入英语成为 social，用来指人与人之间的关系。

items.en: Movere 'to move, set in motion' is the source of mobilis 'easy to move' and mobilitas 'movement, changeableness'. The deeper root is reconstructed, not recorded.
items.cn: movere 意为「移动、使动」，是 mobilis「易于移动」与 mobilitas「移动、易变」的来源。更深的词根属重构形式，并无直接记录。

items.en: Mobilitas in classical Latin covered both physical movement and changeableness of fortune, which is the bridge to rank and class.
items.cn: 古典拉丁中的 mobilitas 既指身体的移动，也指命运的无常，这正是通向等级与阶层的桥梁。

items.en: Both social and mobility were in English by the seventeenth century; their fixed pairing belongs to twentieth-century sociology, when census records made movement between occupations comparable.
items.cn: social 与 mobility 到 17 世纪都已进入英语；两者的固定搭配属于 20 世纪社会学，当时普查记录使职业之间的移动可以比较。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origins and first date): the pre-Latin origin of socius and the root behind movere are reconstructions, and the first use of the exact compound is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：socius 在拉丁语之前的来源、movere 的词根均属重构形式；这一确切组合的最早使用没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds sociological terms that share the adjective social but name conditions rather than movement; group two holds terms for movement itself.
note.cn: 第一组是共享「社会的」这一形容词的社会学术语，但它们指的是状态而非移动；第二组才是表示移动本身的说法。

entries.definition: The unequal distribution of income, schooling and opportunity; people can be unequal without moving at all.
entries.definitionCN: 收入、教育与机会分配不均；人们可以完全不移动而依然不平等。

entries.definition: The layered ordering of a society into strata; mobility is the traffic between those layers.
entries.definitionCN: 社会被分成层层叠叠的等级；流动则是在这些层之间来往。

entries.definition: A broad grouping by wealth, education and occupation; class is where someone stands, mobility is the move.
entries.definitionCN: 按财富、教育与职业划分的大类；阶级是人所在的位置，流动是移动。

entries.definition: Resources gained through networks and trust; it shares the adjective but not the idea of changing rank.
entries.definitionCN: 通过关系网络与信任获得的资源；只共享形容词，与等级变动无关。

entries.definition: A near synonym that stresses movement between classes instead of between positions in general.
entries.definitionCN: 近义说法，强调在阶级之间移动，而非泛指位置变动。

entries.definition: Movement in income or wealth, which is one measurable strand of social mobility.
entries.definitionCN: 收入或财富的变动，是社会流动中可测量的一条线索。

entries.definition: Plain-language phrasing for upward movement, often carrying a moral glow of deserved success.
entries.definitionCN: 向上移动的日常说法，常带「理应成功」的道德色彩。

entries.definition: Movement between jobs and levels inside a working life; narrower than the full sociological phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 职业生涯内部职位与层级的移动；范围比完整的社会学术语更窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Social plus mobility: a rank is a square a person can move out of.
normal.cn: 社会加可移动性：等级就像一格，人可以换到别的格。

normal.en: The fixed phrases upward and downward write the direction into the term.
normal.cn: 固定说法向上与向下直接把方向写进了术语。

normal.en: Intergenerational compares parents with children; intragenerational stays inside one life.
normal.cn: 代际比较的是父母与子女；代内则停留在一个人的一生之内。

normal.en: Structural mobility reminds you that the number of good jobs can grow for everyone at once.
normal.cn: 结构流动提醒：好职位的总量可以同时为所有人增加。

normal.en: Occupation is the usual measuring rod, because censuses record jobs far more reliably than prestige.
normal.cn: 职业是常用的量尺，因为普查记录职业远比记录声望可靠。

abstract.en: Picture a lift that stops at a different floor for each generation of one family.
abstract.cn: 想象一部电梯，在一家人的每一代停在不同楼层。

abstract.en: Picture a race where the starting lines are drawn at different distances from the finish.
abstract.cn: 想象一场赛跑，每个人的起跑线离终点远近不同。

abstract.en: Picture a chess piece that changes squares without changing its colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚棋子换了格子，却没有换颜色。

examples.en: The report found that social mobility had stalled for the poorest fifth of the population.
examples.cn: 报告发现，最贫穷的五分之一人口的社会流动已经停滞。

examples.en: Free schooling is often defended as an engine of social mobility.
examples.cn: 免费教育常被辩护为社会流动的引擎。

examples.en: Comparisons of social mobility across regions must allow for the cost of housing.
examples.cn: 比较各区域的社会流动时，必须考虑住房成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「社会的（social）+ 可动性（mobility）」——人在社会阶梯上换位置，就是社会流动

root: 拉丁 socius「同伴、盟友」经 socialis 得 social；拉丁 movere「移动」经 mobilis、mobilitas 得 mobility；两词在近代社会学中固定连用。socius 与 movere 的更深来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one figure: a person standing on a rung of a social ladder, moving up or down, compared with parents, followed through a working life, channelled through occupation, and finally counted as a rate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形象展开：一个人站在社会阶梯的某一格，向上或向下移动，与父母比较，贯穿一生，经由职业实现，最后被折算成比率。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ladder whose rungs are social positions, with people stepping between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架以社会位置为横档的梯子，人们在其间换步。

branches.en: POSITION: the base sense, a move from one rank to another in either direction.
branches.cn: 位置：基础义，从一个等级移动到另一个，方向不限。

branches.en: DIRECTION: upward and downward name the two arrows that the bare noun leaves open.
branches.cn: 方向：向上与向下标出裸名词未定的两支箭头。

branches.en: TIME SCALE: parents to children, or one person across a working life.
branches.cn: 时间尺度：从父母到子女，或一个人跨越职业生涯。

branches.en: CHANNEL: occupation is the track along which most movement is actually observed.
branches.cn: 通道：职业是实际观察到的大部分移动所走的轨道。

branches.en: SHAPE AND COUNT: the economy can lift a whole cohort, and the result can be measured as a rate.
branches.cn: 结构与计量：经济可以整体抬升一代人，结果又能折算成比率。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two Latin-derived words, each with a prefix-free root and a productive suffix, so the whole expression can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个源自拉丁语的词构成，各自包含一个词根与一个能产后缀，因此整个表达可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius and movere supply the two roots; the suffixes -al and -ity turn them into an adjective and a noun, and the same roots recur in many English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 与 movere 提供两个词根；后缀 -al 与 -ity 分别把它们变成形容词与名词，这两个词根还出现在许多英语词中。

items.example: The root names the people one is bound to.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指与自己结伴、相互绑定的人。

items.example: It turns a noun of companionship into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把表示同伴关系的名词变成形容词。

items.example: Social ties bind neighbours into a group.
items.exampleCN: 社会纽带把邻里绑成一个群体。

items.example: The root carries the idea of setting something in motion.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「使某物动起来」的意思。

items.example: It forms the adjective of easy movement.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「易于移动」的形容词。

items.example: A mobile workforce follows the jobs.
items.exampleCN: 可流动的劳动力会跟着工作走。

items.example: It turns the adjective of movement into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把表示移动的形容词变成名词。

items.example: Mobility of labour is high in the coastal cities.
items.exampleCN: 沿海城市的劳动力流动性很高。

items.example: The union mobilized its members for the vote.
items.exampleCN: 工会动员会员参加投票。

items.meaning: the act of setting in motion
items.example: Mobilization of reserves took three days.
items.exampleCN: 预备役的调动用了三天。

derivatives.zh: 可移动的 / 移动电话

definition_zh: 流动性；移动能力；（人或资源在地方、职业、阶层之间的）流动
definition_en: the ability or tendency to move, or the movement of people between places, jobs or social positions
core_image: 同一个人分别拄着助行器挪向车站、拖着箱子搬到另一座城、从车间走进办公室，三条路线并排出现
scene: 雨后的车站里，一位拄拐的老人慢慢挪向站台边。Mobility is the first thing a physiotherapist works to restore after a stroke.
sceneCN: 这里 mobility 指「身体活动的能力」（第 1 个义项：行动自如的能力）；句意为中风之后，康复师最先着手恢复的是活动能力。图中可辨识物件：拐杖、站台边沿、康复训练带、三条并行路线。

pos.zh: 流动性；移动能力（不可数；指具体某类流动时可作可数）

derivatives.zh: 可移动的 / 移动电话

senses.title: Physical ability to move
senses.definition: the power of a person to move the body, especially to walk or shift position
senses.definitionCN: 一个人移动身体的能力，尤指行走或变换姿势
senses.example: Mobility is the first thing a physiotherapist works to restore after a stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 中风之后，康复师最先着手恢复的是活动能力。
senses.why: mobility comes from a Latin word for being movable, so the body is the most literal thing that can be mobile.
senses.whyCN: mobility 源自拉丁语中「可移动」的说法，因此身体是最字面意义上的可动之物。

senses.title: Ability to travel or be transported
senses.definition: the ease with which people or goods can reach places
senses.definitionCN: 人或货物抵达各地点的便利程度
senses.example: The new tram line gave the district a mobility it had never had.
senses.exampleCN: 新有轨电车线给了这个城区从未有过的出行便利。
senses.why: once movement is supplied by vehicles, the word shifts from the body to the journey.
senses.whyCN: 当移动由交通工具提供时，这个词便从身体转到旅程上。

senses.title: Movement between social positions
senses.definition: the movement of people between social classes or ranks
senses.definitionCN: 人们在社阶层之间或等级之间的移动
senses.example: Education is the strongest single lever of mobility in the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 在这项调查中，教育是撬动社会流动最强的一根杠杆。
senses.why: a society can be imagined as a ladder, and mobility is the traffic up and down it.
senses.whyCN: 社会可以被想象成一架梯子，流动就是上上下下的往来。

senses.title: Movement between jobs
senses.definition: the frequency with which workers change jobs, employers or trades
senses.definitionCN: 劳动者更换工作、雇主或行业的频繁程度
senses.example: Job mobility is high in hospitality, where contracts are short.
senses.exampleCN: 餐饮住宿业合同期短，职业流动很高。
senses.why: occupation is the everyday channel through which social movement is actually observed.
senses.whyCN: 职业是实际观察社会流动时最日常的通道。

senses.title: Movement between places
senses.definition: the movement of people from one place or region to another
senses.definitionCN: 人们从一个地方或地区移动到另一个
senses.example: Residential mobility falls sharply once families own their homes.
senses.exampleCN: 家庭一旦拥有自有住房，迁居流动就明显下降。
senses.why: migration is mobility written on a map, so the word covers changing address as well as changing class.
senses.whyCN: 迁移是画在地图上的流动，因此这个词既涵盖换阶层，也涵盖换住址。

senses.title: Movement of labour and capital
senses.definition: the freedom of workers, money or resources to move to where they are most useful
senses.definitionCN: 工人、资金或资源流向最有用处的自由程度
senses.example: Capital mobility lets savings cross borders in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 资本流动让储蓄在几秒内跨越国境。
senses.why: economists generalized the idea from people to any input that can be shifted between uses.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把这个概念从人推广到任何可在用途之间转移的投入。

senses.title: Charge-carrier mobility in physics
senses.titleCN: 物理学中的载流子迁移率
senses.definition: a measure of how quickly electrons or other charge carriers drift through a material under a field
senses.definitionCN: 在电场作用下，电子等载流子在材料中漂移快慢的量度
senses.example: Silicon has a lower electron mobility than gallium arsenide.
senses.exampleCN: 硅的电子迁移率比砷化镓低。
senses.why: the technical sense keeps the literal core: how easily the carriers can move through the lattice.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义保留了字面核心：载流子在晶格中移动的容易程度。

senses.title: Tactical mobility in warfare
senses.definition: the ability of troops or equipment to move quickly into position
senses.definitionCN: 部队或装备快速进入位置的能力
senses.example: The brigade traded armour for mobility on the mountain roads.
senses.exampleCN: 该旅在山路上用装甲换取机动性。
senses.why: military planners want the same thing the word names everywhere: movement without delay.
senses.whyCN: 军事规划者想要的，正是这个词到处所指的东西：不受耽搁的移动。

intro.en: Mobility comes from Latin mobilitas 'movement, changeableness', formed on mobilis 'movable', which in turn rests on movere 'to move'. It entered English through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mobility 来自拉丁 mobilitas「移动、易变」，由 mobilis「可移动」构成，而 mobilis 又出自 movere「移动」。它经古法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Movere meant 'to move, set in motion'. Its deeper root is reconstructed rather than attested, and the form commonly quoted for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: movere 意为「移动、使动」。其更深词根属重构形式而非直接记录，常被引用的那个印欧形式也只是重构。

items.en: Mobilis 'movable, flexible, changeable' was used of bodies, property and minds alike, already widening the sense beyond mere travel.
items.cn: mobilis 意为「可移动的、灵活的、易变的」，既用于身体，也用于财产与心思，其含义早已超出单纯的行走。

items.en: Mobilitas named both physical movement and the fickleness of fortune, a pairing that later made social rank a natural extension.
items.cn: mobilitas 既指身体的移动，也指命运的无常，这种并置后来使社会等级的引申显得自然。

items.en: Old French mobilite carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first as a word for movement and mutability.
items.cn: 古法语 mobilite 在 14 世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指移动与无常。

items.en: Industrial and social change gave the word its familiar modern uses: movement of workers, of families and of classes, and later the drift of electrons in a solid.
items.cn: 工业与社会变迁赋予它熟悉的现代用法：工人、家庭与阶层的移动，后来又加上电子在固体中的漂移。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the Indo-European root behind movere is a reconstruction, and no attested earlier form of the word survives.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：movere 背后的印欧词根属重构形式，该词没有更早的有据可查形式流传下来。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same root that look confusingly alike; group two holds words for movement with a narrower reach.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一词根、外形极易混淆的词；第二组是表示移动但范围更窄的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning able to move, and a noun for a telephone that moves with its owner; it is not the abstract noun of movement.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词指可移动的，作名词指随身携带的电话；它不是表示抽象流动的名词。

entries.definition: To set people or resources in motion for a purpose; the verb names the act, not the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个目的把人或资源调动起来；动词指动作，不指能力。

entries.definition: From mutare 'to change', not movere: it means susceptibility to change, often in biology or law.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 mutare「改变」而非 movere：指易受改变的性质，常用于生物学或法律。

entries.definition: The capacity for spontaneous movement in cells or organisms; a technical cousin, not the general social word.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞或生物自发运动的能力；是技术上的近亲，不是泛指的社会用语。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for changing position; it lacks the implication of capacity or rate that mobility carries.
entries.definitionCN: 表示位置改变的日常名词；不含 mobility 所带的「能力或比率」意味。

entries.definition: Movement produced by the organism itself, used of sperm, bacteria or gut muscle rather than of people in a society.
entries.definitionCN: 由生物自身产生的运动，用于精子、细菌或肠道肌肉，而非社会中的人。

entries.definition: The ability to bend or adapt to new conditions; it overlaps with mobility only when the change is one of position or job.
entries.definitionCN: 弯曲或适应新条件的能力；只有当变化涉及位置或工作时，才与 mobility 重叠。

entries.definition: Movement caused by something else pushing or removing; it usually implies loss of a former place.
entries.definitionCN: 由外力推走或移走造成的移动；通常意味着失去原来的位置。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real root, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented sound-alikes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词，而非编造的谐音。

normal.en: The root means move, so mobility is the capacity to be moved or to move.
normal.cn: 词根意为移动，因此 mobility 就是能被移动或自行移动的能力。

normal.en: Labour mobility, social mobility and geographic mobility mark the three main fields.
normal.cn: 劳动力流动、社会流动与地理流动标出三大领域。

normal.en: A mobility aid is literally a device that gives movement back.
normal.cn: 助行器具字面上就是一件把移动能力还给人的装置。

normal.en: Mobile, mobilize and mobilization all share the same root.
normal.cn: 同族的「移动的」「动员」「动员化」等形式共用同一个词根。

normal.en: In physics the word keeps the literal sense: how easily carriers move.
normal.cn: 在物理学中这个词保持字面义：载流子移动的容易程度。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens in three directions: to the street, to another class and to another job.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门朝三个方向打开：通向街道、通向另一个阶层、通向另一份工作。

abstract.en: Picture water that finds every gap in a wall, never staying where it was put.
abstract.cn: 想象水穿过墙上的每一道缝，从不停在被放置的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder leaning against a building that is itself being rebuilt.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子靠在正在重建的建筑上。

examples.en: The study links residential mobility to the length of a daily commute.
examples.cn: 这项研究把迁居流动与每日通勤距离联系起来。

examples.en: Labour mobility across the border fell after the visa rules changed.
examples.cn: 签证规则改变后，跨境劳动力流动下降了。

examples.en: Improved mobility in the knee was the main goal of the treatment.
examples.cn: 治疗的主要目标是改善膝关节的活动度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸吧·力」——一摸就能动起来的能力，就是移动能力与流动性

root: 拉丁 movere「移动」→ mobilis「可移动的」→ mobilitas「移动、易变」；经古法语进入英语为 mobility。movere 的更深词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one capacity: a body that can move, a person who can reach places, a worker who can change jobs, a class that can rise, capital that can cross borders, carriers that drift through a crystal, and troops that can reach the ridge.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一种能力辐射开来：能动的身体、能抵达各处的人、能换工作的劳动者、能上升的阶层、能跨越国境的资本、能在晶体中漂移的载流子，以及能抵达山脊的部队。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same person moving along three routes at once, by foot, by train and up a job ladder.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个人同时沿三条路线移动，靠双脚、靠列车，也沿职业阶梯向上。

branches.en: BODY: the most literal sense, the power to move one's own limbs.
branches.cn: 身体：最字面的义项，移动自己肢体的能力。

branches.en: VEHICLE: movement is handed over to transport, so the word comes to mean access to places.
branches.cn: 交通工具：移动交给交通工具完成，词义便转为抵达各地的便利。

branches.en: JOB AND ADDRESS: changing employer and changing town are the two everyday forms of movement.
branches.cn: 工作与住址：换雇主与换城市是移动最日常的两种形式。

branches.en: CLASS AND CAPITAL: people and money both move to where opportunity is higher.
branches.cn: 阶层与资本：人和钱都会流向机会更多的地方。

branches.en: PHYSICS AND WAR: the same capacity measured in a crystal or required on a ridge.
branches.cn: 物理与军事：同一种能力，或在晶体中被计量，或在山脊上被要求。

intro.en: Mobility is one Latin root plus two suffixes, and the whole family can be read from those pieces.
intro.cn: mobility 由一个拉丁词根加两个后缀构成，整个词族都可以按这些成分读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere supplies the root; the suffixes -ilis and -itas shape it first into an adjective and then into a noun of state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 提供词根；后缀 -ilis 与 -itas 先把它构成形容词，再构成表状态的名词。

items.example: The root is the seed of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是整个词族的种子。

items.example: It builds the adjective of capacity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示能力的形容词。

items.example: A mobile clinic reaches the villages.
items.exampleCN: 流动诊所抵达各个村庄。

items.example: It converts the adjective into a state noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词转成表状态的名词。

items.example: Mobility of labour is high in the coastal cities.
items.exampleCN: 沿海城市的劳动力流动性很高。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a verb of action.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表动作的动词。

items.example: They mobilized the volunteers within a day.
items.exampleCN: 他们在一天之内动员了志愿者。

items.meaning: the act of setting in motion
items.example: Mobilization of the reserves began at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 预备役的调动在黎明开始。

items.example: The joint was immobile for six weeks.
items.exampleCN: 这个关节有六周不能活动。

items.example: Long immobility weakens the muscles.
items.exampleCN: 长期不动会使肌肉变弱。

derivatives.zh: 可移动的 / 移动电话

definition_zh: 移民入境；（总称）入境移民；入境查验
definition_en: the act or process of coming to a country in order to live there, or the flow of people who do so
core_image: 机场到达口一条长队，行李箱贴着不同颜色的标签，玻璃门后是等候接机的家人
scene: 海关大厅里，一家人提着行李箱排在队伍末端，孩子紧紧抓着护照。Immigration has reshaped the neighbourhood's shops and schools.
sceneCN: 这里 immigration 指「人口迁入一个国家并定居的过程」（第 1 个义项：入境定居这一行为）；句意为移民入境改变了这个街区的店铺与学校。图中可辨识物件：到达口长队、贴标签的行李箱、护照、接机的人群。

pos.zh: 移民入境；入境移民（不可数；指具体批次时可作可数）

senses.title: The act of settling in a new country
senses.titleCN: 迁入他国并定居的行为
senses.definition: the act of coming to a country that is not one's own in order to live there
senses.definitionCN: 来到并非自己所属的国家并在此生活的行为
senses.example: Immigration has reshaped the neighbourhood's shops and schools.
senses.exampleCN: 移民入境改变了这个街区的店铺与学校。
senses.why: the prefix means into and the root means to move, so immigration is movement inward, seen from the receiving country.
senses.whyCN: 前缀意为「进入」，词根意为「迁移」，因此 immigration 是从接收国角度看到的向内移动。

senses.title: The volume of people arriving
senses.titleCN: 入境移民的总量与流量
senses.definition: the number or flow of people entering a country over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内进入一国的人数或人流
senses.example: Immigration doubled in the decade after the mines opened.
senses.exampleCN: 矿区开工后的十年里，入境移民数量翻了一番。
senses.why: an uncountable noun easily turns into a quantity word, as with traffic or rainfall.
senses.whyCN: 不可数名词很容易转为数量词，就像「交通量」或「降雨量」那样。

senses.title: The border admission process
senses.definition: the official procedure by which a country admits or refuses entrants
senses.definitionCN: 一国准许或拒绝入境者的官方程序
senses.example: The queue at immigration stretched past the baggage hall.
senses.exampleCN: 入境查验的队伍一直排到行李厅之外。
senses.why: the abstract noun metonymically names the desk and the officers that carry the process out.
senses.whyCN: 抽象名词以转喻方式指执行这一程序的服务台与官员。

senses.title: Immigrants taken as a group
senses.definition: the people who have entered a country, considered collectively
senses.definitionCN: 已经进入一国的人，作为整体来看
senses.example: Immigration built the city's garment trade in two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 入境移民在两代人之内建起了这座城市的制衣业。
senses.why: the act stands for the actors, a common shortcut in political speech.
senses.whyCN: 用行为指代行为者，是政治语言中常见的省略。

senses.title: A component of population change
senses.definition: the gain of people from abroad in the accounting of a population
senses.definitionCN: 在人口核算中来自国外的净增人数
senses.example: Natural increase fell, so immigration kept the population growing.
senses.exampleCN: 自然增长下降，因此移民入境维持了人口增长。
senses.why: demographers balance births, deaths, immigration and emigration, and each one is a line in the ledger.
senses.whyCN: 人口学者在出生、死亡、迁入与迁出之间做平衡，每一项都是账簿上的一行。

senses.title: Colonization by a species
senses.definition: the arrival of organisms into a habitat where they were not previously established
senses.definitionCN: 生物进入此前并未立足的栖息地
senses.example: Immigration of new species followed the opening of the canal.
senses.exampleCN: 运河开通之后，新物种随之迁入。
senses.why: ecology borrows the word because individuals arriving and settling is the same pattern at a different scale.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用这个词，因为个体到来并定居，是同一格局在不同尺度上的表现。

senses.title: A historical wave or era
senses.titleCN: 历史上的移民潮与时代
senses.definition: a distinct period or wave in which large numbers of people entered a country
senses.definitionCN: 大批人口进入某国的特定时期或浪潮
senses.example: The great immigration of the 1880s left its mark on the census.
senses.exampleCN: 19 世纪 80 年代的移民大潮在普查中留下了印记。
senses.why: historians turn the process into a countable event when a wave has a clear beginning and end.
senses.whyCN: 当一次浪潮起止清楚时，历史学者会把这一过程变成可计数的事件。

senses.title: A political issue
senses.titleCN: 作为政治议题的移民问题
senses.definition: the framing of entry and settlement as a matter of public dispute and policy
senses.definitionCN: 把入境与定居框定为公共争论与政策问题
senses.example: Immigration dominated the debate in every constituency.
senses.exampleCN: 移民问题在每一个选区都主导了辩论。
senses.why: once the word becomes a topic rather than an event, it can dominate an election without naming any person.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词成为议题而非事件，它就能在未指名任何人的情况下主导一场选举。

intro.en: Immigration rests on Latin immigrare 'to move into', from in- 'into' plus migrare 'to depart, migrate'. The English noun appeared in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: immigration 源于拉丁 immigrare「迁入」，由 in-「进入」与 migrare「离开、迁移」构成。英语名词出现于 17 世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Migrare meant 'to move from one place to another, to change residence'. Its own earlier origin is not established, and the Indo-European root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: migrare 意为「从一处移到另一处、更换居所」。它更早的来源未得到证明，常为其提出的印欧词根属重构形式。

items.en: The preposition in 'into' became a prefix marking motion inward, the mirror of e- or ex- marking motion out.
items.cn: 介词 in「进入」成为前缀，标记向内的移动，与标记向外移动的 e- 或 ex- 正相对。

items.en: In- plus migrare gave immigrare 'to move into a place, to settle there', used of people and later of animals.
items.cn: in- 加 migrare 构成 immigrare「迁入某地并定居」，用于人，后来也用于动物。

items.en: English formed immigration from the stem of immigrate in the seventeenth century, at first for settlement within a country as well as across borders.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪用 immigrate 的词干构成 immigration，最初既指跨国入境，也指一国之内的迁居。

items.en: Border controls and mass shipping in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries narrowed the word to entry into a state, and made it a standard term of policy and demography.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪的边境管控与大规模航运，把这个词收窄为进入国家，并使其成为政策与人口学的标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin history of migrare is unsettled, and the earliest English citation of the noun is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：migrare 在拉丁语之前的历史尚无定论，这个名词的最早英语书证也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the near-identical migration words that differ only by direction; group two holds words for arrival and settlement.
note.cn: 第一组是只差方向的迁移类近形词；第二组是表示到来与定居的说法。

entries.definition: The same movement seen from the country people leave, with e- 'out' instead of in- 'into'.
entries.definitionCN: 同一移动从人们离开的国家看，前缀为「向外」而非「向内」。

entries.definition: Movement from one place to another without specifying whether a border is crossed; it covers birds, workers and data.
entries.definitionCN: 从一地到另一地的移动，不说明是否越过国境；可指鸟类、劳动者与数据。

entries.definition: The person who immigrates; the noun of action and the noun of person are constantly swapped in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 迁入的人；表动作的名词与表人的名词在口语中常被互换。

entries.definition: The person who emigrates, named from the sending side; the same individual can be both terms at once.
entries.definitionCN: 迁出的人，从输出方命名；同一个人可以同时是两个称呼。

entries.definition: A mass arrival of people, money or things; it stresses volume and suddenness rather than the legal act.
entries.definitionCN: 人、钱或物的大量涌入；强调数量与突然性，而非法律行为。

entries.definition: The process of making a permanent home in a new place; it can follow immigration but is not the crossing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 在新地方安家的过程；可以发生在移民之后，但不等于越境本身。

entries.definition: The instant of reaching a place; it says nothing about staying or about official permission.
entries.definitionCN: 到达某地的那一刻；不涉及是否留下或是否获准。

entries.definition: A planned move to a new place, often arranged by authorities for refugees; it is a policy channel of immigration.
entries.definitionCN: 有计划的迁往新地，常由当局为难民安排；是移民入境的一种政策渠道。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real root and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、真实的词根与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means into and the root means move: movement inward.
normal.cn: 前缀意为进入，词根意为迁移：向内的移动。

normal.en: The pair immigration and emigration differ only in the direction of the prefix.
normal.cn: 移民入境与移民出境这一对词，只差前缀的方向。

normal.en: The person noun adds a ending for the one who does it.
normal.cn: 表人的名词加一个表施动者的词尾，指做这件事的人。

normal.en: Fixed phrases such as immigration policy and immigration control belong to the border sense.
normal.cn: 移民政策、入境管控这类固定搭配属于边境义。

normal.en: In demography it is one line in the ledger beside births and deaths.
normal.cn: 在人口学中，它是出生与死亡旁边账簿上的一行。

abstract.en: Picture a one-way door that only opens from the outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇单向门，只能从外面推开。

abstract.en: Picture a river splitting into two channels, one called in and one called out.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河分成两条水道，一条叫进，一条叫出。

abstract.en: Picture a household ledger where one column is arrivals and the opposite column departures.
abstract.cn: 想象一本家庭账簿，一栏记到来，对面一栏记离开。

examples.en: Immigration rose sharply after the labour shortage of the 1950s.
examples.cn: 20 世纪 50 年代劳动力短缺之后，移民入境急剧上升。

examples.en: The ministry published immigration figures for the first quarter.
examples.cn: 该部门公布了第一季度的移民入境数字。

examples.en: Students queued at immigration for nearly two hours.
examples.cn: 学生们在入境查验处排了近两个小时的队。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一民·进来」——一批人进来定居，就是移民入境

root: 拉丁 in-「进入」+ migrare「迁移」→ immigrare「迁入定居」；英语 immigration 于 17 世纪由 immigrate 的词干构成。migrare 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement seen from the receiving side: the act of entry, the volume of arrivals, the desk that checks them, the people themselves, the line in the population ledger, the arrival of a species, a historical wave and a political issue.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从接收方看到的同一次移动展开：入境的行为、到来者的总量、查验的服务台、这些人本身、人口账簿上的一行、物种的到来、历史浪潮与政治议题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue at an arrival gate, each suitcase carrying a life that is about to be unpacked somewhere else.
core.cn: 核心意象：到达口的一条长队，每只行李箱里都装着一段即将在别处展开的生活。

branches.en: CROSSING: the base act of coming in order to stay.
branches.cn: 越境而入：为了留下而进来的基础行为。

branches.en: VOLUME AND WAVE: the flow can be counted, and a counted flow becomes a historical wave.
branches.cn: 总量与浪潮：流量可以被计数，而被计数的流量会成为历史浪潮。

branches.en: CHECKPOINT: the abstract noun stands for the desk and the officers who carry the process out.
branches.cn: 查验口：抽象名词指执行该程序的服务台与官员。

branches.en: THE ARRIVING: people taken as a group, and, in ecology, organisms colonizing a habitat.
branches.cn: 到来者：作为整体的人，以及在生态学中定殖栖息的生物。

branches.en: LEDGER AND DEBATE: one line in population accounting, and one topic in public argument.
branches.cn: 账簿与争论：人口核算中的一行，也是公共争论中的一个议题。

intro.en: Immigration is a prefix, a root and a suffix, and the same pieces build the whole migration family.
intro.cn: immigration 由一个前缀、一个词根与一个后缀构成，同样的成分也构成整个迁移词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- marks motion inward, migrare supplies the root of moving, and -ation turns the verb into an action noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 in- 标记向内移动，migrare 提供「迁移」的词根，-ation 把动词变成表动作的名词。

items.example: The prefix directs the movement toward the receiving country.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把移动朝向接收国。

items.meaning: move from one place to another
items.example: The root supplies the idea of changing residence.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供更换居所的意思。

items.example: Her grandparents immigrated in the 1930s.
items.exampleCN: 她的祖父母在 20 世纪 30 年代迁入。

items.example: It builds the person noun from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词构成表人的名词。

items.meaning: a person who moves into a country
items.example: The first immigrant on the list arrived in 1848.
items.exampleCN: 名单上的第一位移民于 1848 年抵达。

items.example: It turns the verb into the name of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成过程之名。

items.meaning: the process of moving into a country
items.example: Immigration filled the mills with new workers.
items.exampleCN: 移民入境为工厂填满了新工人。

items.example: The opposite prefix names the same movement from the other end.
items.exampleCN: 相反的前缀从另一端为同一移动命名。

items.meaning: to move out of a country
items.example: The family emigrated in search of work.
items.exampleCN: 这家人为寻找工作而迁出。

items.example: Bird migration follows the seasons.
items.exampleCN: 鸟类迁徙随季节而行。

definition_zh: 移民；迁入者；（作定语）移民的
definition_en: a person who comes to a country in order to live there permanently
core_image: 一只旧皮箱里整齐叠着故乡的照片、一沓证件和一件一直没舍得穿的新外套
scene: 社区厨房里，几位新邻居端着各自家乡的菜，用不太熟练的当地话介绍自己的名字。The immigrant opened a small bakery that soon became the street's meeting place.
sceneCN: 这里 immigrant 指「迁入某国并长期定居的人」（第 1 个义项：从外国来此定居的人）；句意为这位移民开了一间小面包店，很快成了这条街聚会的去处。图中可辨识物件：旧皮箱、家乡照片、证件、面包柜台。

pos.zh: 移民的；迁入者的（作定语，如移民工人）

senses.title: A person settling in a new country
senses.definition: someone who has come to a country in order to make a permanent home there
senses.definitionCN: 来到某国并打算在那里永久安家的人
senses.example: The immigrant opened a small bakery that soon became the street's meeting place.
senses.exampleCN: 这位移民开了一间小面包店，很快成了这条街聚会的去处。
senses.why: the word is the person noun of the verb meaning to move in, so it names the one who has made the crossing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「迁入」动词的人称名词，指完成那次越境的人。

senses.title: A recent arrival
senses.definition: a person who has arrived recently and is still settling in
senses.definitionCN: 刚到不久、仍在安顿中的人
senses.example: The clinic offers translation for immigrants in their first year.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所为入境第一年的新居民提供翻译。
senses.why: the line between newcomer and settler is a matter of time, and everyday usage often means the former.
senses.whyCN: 新来者与定居者之间只差时间，日常用法常指前者。

senses.title: Used before a noun
senses.definition: used attributively to describe workers, families, neighbourhoods or services connected with immigrants
senses.definitionCN: 作定语，描述与移民有关的工人、家庭、社区或服务
senses.example: Immigrant families gathered at the school gate on the first day.
senses.exampleCN: 开学第一天，移民家庭聚在校门口。
senses.why: English readily uses a person noun as a modifier, so the noun doubles as an adjective without changing form.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把人称名词直接当修饰语，因此这个词不改形就兼作形容词。

senses.title: Legal status: documented or not
senses.definition: a person classified by whether the state has recognized their right to remain
senses.definitionCN: 按国家是否承认其居留权来分类的人
senses.example: Undocumented immigrants avoid clinics that ask for papers.
senses.exampleCN: 无证件移民会避开要求出示证件的诊所。
senses.why: once entry is controlled, the person is also a legal category, and the adjective in front decides which.
senses.whyCN: 一旦入境受管控，人也成为一个法律类别，前面的形容词决定属于哪一类。

senses.title: An economic or labour migrant
senses.definition: a person who moves primarily to find work or higher pay
senses.definitionCN: 主要为寻找工作或更高报酬而迁移的人
senses.example: The harvest relies on immigrant labour from across the border.
senses.exampleCN: 收割依赖来自境外的移民劳动力。
senses.why: labour demand is one of the oldest engines of settlement, so the word often carries an economic motive.
senses.whyCN: 劳动力需求是定居最古老的引擎之一，因此这个词常带经济动机。

senses.title: A broad label covering refugees
senses.definition: in loose usage, anyone who has moved to a new country, including those who fled rather than chose
senses.definitionCN: 宽松用法中指任何迁入新国家的人，包括被迫逃离而非自愿选择者
senses.example: The centre calls them immigrants, though many hold refugee status.
senses.exampleCN: 中心把他们称作移民，尽管其中许多人有难民身份。
senses.why: everyday speech lumps all arrivals under one word, while legal language keeps refugee and immigrant apart.
senses.whyCN: 日常语言把所有到来者归入一个词，法律语言却把难民与移民分开。

senses.title: Loose use for the second generation
senses.definition: a child of immigrants, often called an immigrant although born in the country
senses.definitionCN: 移民的子女，虽在本国出生却常被称作移民
senses.example: She is called an immigrant although she was born in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她虽在这座城市出生，却被称作移民。
senses.why: the label follows the family's origin rather than the individual's birthplace, a usage that sociologists usually avoid.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签跟随家庭出身而非个人出生地，社会学者通常避免这种用法。

senses.title: A colonizing species in ecology
senses.definition: an organism that has arrived in a habitat from elsewhere and established itself there
senses.definitionCN: 从别处到达某栖息地并在此立足的生物
senses.example: The immigrant species displaced two native grasses within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这一迁入物种在十年内挤掉了两种本地禾草。
senses.why: ecology applies the human word to any individual arriving in a new range, keeping the same core of settling.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把这个指人的词用于任何到达新分布区的个体，保留「落脚定居」这一核心。

intro.en: Immigrant is the present participle stem of Latin immigrare 'to move into', from in- 'into' and migrare 'to migrate'. English took it from French in the eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: immigrant 是拉丁 immigrare「迁入」的现在分词词干，由 in-「进入」与 migrare「迁移」构成。英语在 18 世纪经法语吸收。年代均为约数。

items.en: Migrare meant 'to move from place to place, to change one's dwelling'. Its earlier origin is unsettled, and any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: migrare 意为「从一处迁到另一处、更换住所」。它更早的来源尚无定论，为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式。

items.en: In- 'into' plus migrare gave immigrare 'to move into a place and settle'. The participle immigrans described a person in the act of doing so.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 migrare 构成 immigrare「迁入并定居」，其分词 immigrans 描述正在这样做的人。

items.en: French immigrant carried the participle into English as a noun for the person, while immigration named the process.
items.cn: 法语 immigrant 把这个分词带入英语，作指人的名词，而 immigration 指整个过程。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the noun was used both for settlers and, in colonial records, for anyone arriving under that heading.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，这个名词既指定居者，也在殖民记录中泛指以此名目到来的人。

items.en: Passport control and nationality law in the twentieth century made the word a legal category with documented and undocumented variants.
items.cn: 20 世纪的护照管控与国籍法，使这个词成为带有「有证」「无证」变体的法律类别。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin history of migrare is not established, and the earliest English citation is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：migrare 在拉丁语之前的历史未得到证明，最早的英语书证也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the direction words that differ by a single prefix; group two holds other names for people who arrive.
note.cn: 第一组是只差一个前缀的方向词；第二组是对到来者的其他称呼。

entries.definition: The person who leaves, with the prefix meaning out; one individual can be an emigrant and an immigrant at the same time.
entries.definitionCN: 离开的人，前缀意为向外；同一个人可以同时既是迁出者又是迁入者。

entries.definition: A person or animal that moves from one place to another, with no prefix and therefore no direction; it also covers internal movement.
entries.definitionCN: 从一地移到另一地的人或动物，没有前缀因而没有方向；也涵盖国内流动。

entries.definition: The process or flow of entry, not a single person; the two nouns are often confused in political speech.
entries.definitionCN: 入境的过程或流量，不是单个人；两个名词在政治语言中常被混淆。

entries.definition: To leave one country for another; the verb looks at the departure rather than the arrival.
entries.definitionCN: 离开一国前往另一国；动词着眼的是离境而非抵达。

entries.definition: Anyone who has recently arrived, in a village or a workplace; it need not involve a national border.
entries.definitionCN: 任何最近到来的人，可在村庄或工作场所；不一定涉及国境。

entries.definition: A person who takes land and builds a permanent home, often in a colonial or frontier setting.
entries.definitionCN: 占据土地并建立永久居所的人，常用于殖民或边疆背景。

entries.definition: A person from another country; the word says nothing about whether they have settled or intend to.
entries.definitionCN: 来自另一国的人；不说明是否已经或打算定居。

entries.definition: A person outside their country because of persecution or war, with a protected legal status that immigrant does not imply.
entries.definitionCN: 因迫害或战争而离开本国的人，拥有受保护的法律身份，而移民一词不含此义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real root and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、真实的词根与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means into: the immigrant is the person at the inward end of the crossing.
normal.cn: 前缀意为进入：移民就是这次越境向内的一端的那个人。

normal.en: The pair immigrant and emigrant differ only in the direction of the prefix.
normal.cn: 迁入者与迁出者这一对词，只差前缀的方向。

normal.en: The person noun ends in a suffix that marks the one performing the action.
normal.cn: 指人的名词以一个标记施动者的词尾收束。

normal.en: Fixed phrases such as immigrant worker and immigrant family show the attributive use.
normal.cn: 移民工人、移民家庭这类固定搭配展示了定语用法。

normal.en: In ecology the same noun names a species that arrives and stays.
normal.cn: 在生态学中，同一个名词指到来并留下的物种。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase whose label has been written over twice, old address under new.
abstract.cn: 想象一只行李箱的标签被写过两次，新地址盖住旧地址。

abstract.en: Picture a plant that takes root in a crack of foreign stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物在异乡石头的裂缝里扎根。

abstract.en: Picture a name that follows a family across a map but never quite fits the birthplace.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字跟着家庭跨过地图，却始终与出生地对不上。

examples.en: The city's immigrant population has doubled since the factory opened.
examples.cn: 自工厂开工以来，这座城市的移民人口翻了一番。

examples.en: An immigrant doctor was the first to staff the rural clinic.
examples.cn: 一位移民医生最先为这所乡村诊所配备了人手。

examples.en: The law distinguishes an immigrant from a refugee.
examples.cn: 法律把移民与难民区分开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一民·格兰特」——一位民来到新国家扎根，就是移民

root: 拉丁 in-「进入」+ migrare「迁移」→ immigrare「迁入定居」，取其现在分词词干加人称词尾得 immigrant。migrare 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person: someone who crosses in and stays, a newcomer still settling, a modifier before a noun, a legal status, a labourer, a broad label, a loosely labelled child of settlers, and an organism taking root in a new range.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个人展开：越境而入并留下的人、仍在安顿的新来者、名词前的修饰语、一种法律身份、一名劳动者、一个宽泛标签、被宽松称呼的移民子女，以及在新分布区扎根的生物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a suitcase packed with a photograph, papers and one unworn coat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着照片、证件和一件没穿过的新外套的行李箱。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the base sense, the one who has crossed and settled.
branches.cn: 人本身：基础义，越境并定居的那一个。

branches.en: TIME: the same person seen in the first months, still a newcomer.
branches.cn: 时间：同一个人被看在最初几个月里，仍是新来者。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the noun works as a modifier without changing shape.
branches.cn: 语法：这个名词不改形就能充当修饰语。

branches.en: STATUS AND MOTIVE: papers decide the category, and work often decides the journey.
branches.cn: 身份与动机：证件决定类别，工作往往决定旅程。

branches.en: WIDER LABELS: the word stretches to refugees, to the second generation and to colonizing species.
branches.cn: 更宽的标签：这个词延伸到难民、第二代与定殖物种。

intro.en: Immigrant is a prefix, a root and a person suffix, and the same pieces build the migration family.
intro.cn: immigrant 由一个前缀、一个词根与一个表人后缀构成，同样的成分构成整个迁移词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- marks motion inward, migrare supplies the root of moving, and the participle ending -ant turns the verb into the name of the person.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 in- 标记向内移动，migrare 提供「迁移」的词根，分词词尾 -ant 把动词变成指人的名词。

items.example: The prefix points the movement toward the new country.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把移动指向新的国家。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of leaving one place for another.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供离开一地前往另一地的意思。

items.example: They immigrated with three children.
items.exampleCN: 他们带着三个孩子迁入。

items.example: It turns the verb into a name for the person.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成指人的名词。

items.example: The immigrant registered at the town hall.
items.exampleCN: 这位移民在市政厅登记。

items.example: It turns the verb into the name of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成过程之名。

items.example: Immigration changed the school's language mix.
items.exampleCN: 移民入境改变了这所学校的语言构成。

items.example: It forms the adjective of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示这一过程的形容词。

items.example: The immigratory flow slowed in winter.
items.exampleCN: 迁入的流量在冬季放缓。

items.example: Migration can be internal or international.
items.exampleCN: 迁移可以是国内的，也可以是跨国的。

definition_zh: 移居出境；迁出；（总称）迁出者
definition_en: the act of leaving one's own country in order to settle in another, or the flow of people who do so
core_image: 码头边一只贴旧地址的行李箱，船票印着目的港，身后屋顶渐渐变成一条细线
scene: 小镇车站的告示牌下，年轻人提着行李与父母拥抱告别。Emigration from the region peaked in the years after the harvest failed.
sceneCN: 这里 emigration 指「离开本国到他国定居的行为」（第 1 个义项：迁出本国）；句意为这个地区的向外移民在歉收之后的几年里达到顶峰。图中可辨识物件：贴旧地址的行李箱、船票、远去的屋顶、告示牌。

pos.zh: 移居出境；迁出（不可数；指具体批次时可作可数）

senses.title: Leaving one's country to settle elsewhere
senses.definition: the act of departing from one's own country with the intention of living in another
senses.definitionCN: 离开本国并打算在他国生活的行为
senses.example: Emigration from the region peaked in the years after the harvest failed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区的向外移民在歉收之后的几年里达到顶峰。
senses.why: the prefix means out and the root means move, so emigration is the same crossing seen from the country people leave.
senses.whyCN: 前缀意为向外，词根意为迁移，因此 emigration 是从人们离开的国家看到的同一次越境。

senses.title: The volume of departures
senses.titleCN: 迁出人口的总量与流量
senses.definition: the number or flow of people leaving a country over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内离开一国的人数或人流
senses.example: Emigration doubled while the mines were closing.
senses.exampleCN: 矿区陆续关闭时，外迁人数翻了一番。
senses.why: the uncountable noun works like a quantity word, as with traffic or rainfall.
senses.whyCN: 这个不可数名词起数量词的作用，就像交通量或降雨量。

senses.title: A component of population change
senses.definition: the loss of people to other countries in the accounting of a population
senses.definitionCN: 在人口核算中流向其他国家而减少的人数
senses.example: Net emigration has kept the island's population flat.
senses.exampleCN: 净迁出使这个岛上的人口保持持平。
senses.why: demographers set emigration against immigration in the same ledger of gains and losses.
senses.whyCN: 人口学者把迁出与迁入放在同一本得失账簿的两侧。

senses.title: The departure side of a diaspora
senses.titleCN: 侨民社群形成时的离开一端
senses.definition: the outflow that builds communities of former residents abroad
senses.definitionCN: 在海外形成原居民社群的那股流出
senses.example: Emigration from the valley built three churches in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 从这个山谷的向外移民在首都建起了三座教堂。
senses.why: the same movement that empties one place fills another, and the sending side keeps the name emigration.
senses.whyCN: 同一次移动使一处变空、另一处变满，输出方保留 emigration 这个名字。

senses.title: State policy on leaving
senses.definition: official rules that restrict, permit or encourage citizens to leave
senses.definitionCN: 限制、允许或鼓励公民离开的官方规定
senses.example: Emigration controls were relaxed only in the 1980s.
senses.exampleCN: 出境限制直到 20 世纪 80 年代才放宽。
senses.why: states can control exits as well as entries, so the word also names a policy field.
senses.whyCN: 国家既能管控入境也能管控出境，因此这个词也指一个政策领域。

senses.title: A historical wave
senses.definition: a distinct period in which large numbers of people left a country
senses.definitionCN: 大批人口离开某国的特定时期
senses.example: The great emigration of the 1840s changed the census for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 19 世纪 40 年代的移民大潮在一个世纪里改变了普查数据。
senses.why: a wave with a clear beginning and end becomes a countable historical event.
senses.whyCN: 起止清楚的浪潮会成为可计数的历史事件。

senses.title: Dispersal out of a population
senses.definition: the departure of individuals from a population into new areas
senses.definitionCN: 个体离开原种群进入新区域
senses.example: Emigration of young wolves keeps the pack from growing.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻狼群的迁出使这个群体不致过大。
senses.why: ecology names the outgoing half of dispersal with the same word, while immigration names the incoming half.
senses.whyCN: 生态学用同一个词命名扩散中出去的一半，而迁入命名进来的一半。

senses.title: Relocation to a lower-tax jurisdiction
senses.definition: the movement of wealthy individuals to a place with lower taxes
senses.definitionCN: 富裕个人迁往税负更低的地方
senses.example: Tax emigration drained the capital of its largest investors.
senses.exampleCN: 为避税而迁居使首都失去了最大的投资者。
senses.why: modern finance uses the word for money and its owners moving jurisdiction, echoing the older sense of leaving home.
senses.whyCN: 现代金融用这个词指资金及其所有者更换税区，回响着较早的「离乡」义。

intro.en: Emigration rests on Latin emigrare 'to move out', from e- or ex- 'out' plus migrare 'to migrate'. The English noun appeared in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: emigration 源于拉丁 emigrare「迁出」，由 e- 或 ex-「向外」与 migrare「迁移」构成。英语名词出现于 17 世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Migrare meant 'to move, change one's dwelling'. Its own earlier origin is not established, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: migrare 意为「迁移、更换住所」。它更早的来源未得到证明，为其提出的词根属重构形式。

items.en: The prefix e- or ex- meant 'out of', and it marks the direction away from the starting country.
items.cn: 前缀 e- 或 ex- 意为「向外」，标记离开出发国的方向。

items.en: E- plus migrare gave emigrare 'to move out of a place', the mirror of immigrare 'to move into'.
items.cn: e- 加 migrare 构成 emigrare「迁出某地」，与 immigrare「迁入」正好互为镜像。

items.en: English formed emigration on the stem of emigrate in the seventeenth century, at first for any departure, later chiefly for departure across a national border.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪用 emigrate 的词干构成 emigration，最初泛指离开，后来主要指跨越国境的离开。

items.en: Nineteenth-century shipping records and twentieth-century border controls made the word a standard demographic measure, paired with immigration.
items.cn: 19 世纪的航运记录与 20 世纪的边境管控，使这个词成为标准的人口学指标，并与迁入配对使用。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin history of migrare is unsettled, and the earliest English citation is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：migrare 在拉丁语之前的历史尚无定论，最早的英语书证也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the direction words that differ by one prefix; group two holds words for mass departure.
note.cn: 第一组是只差一个前缀的方向词；第二组是表示大规模离开的说法。

entries.definition: The same movement seen from the receiving country, with in- 'into' instead of e- 'out'.
entries.definitionCN: 同一移动从接收国看，前缀为「向内」而非「向外」。

entries.definition: Movement between places with no border specified; it covers internal moves, birds and even data.
entries.definitionCN: 未说明国境的位移；涵盖国内迁移、鸟类乃至数据。

entries.definition: The person who leaves; the action noun and the person noun are frequently swapped in careless speech.
entries.definitionCN: 离开的人；表动作的名词与表人的名词在随意言谈中常被互换。

entries.definition: To move into a country; the verb faces the destination, while emigrate faces the origin.
entries.definitionCN: 移入某国；这个动词朝向目的地，而迁出动词朝向原籍。

entries.definition: A large departure of people, often sudden and driven by hardship; it stresses the crowd rather than the legal act.
entries.definitionCN: 大批人的离开，常突然且由困境推动；强调人群而非法律行为。

entries.definition: The act of leaving a place, whether or not a new country is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 离开某地的行为，不论是否涉及新的国家。

entries.definition: Moving one's home or business to a new place; it is neutral about borders and motives.
entries.definitionCN: 把住所或企业迁到新地方；对国境与动机都保持中性。

entries.definition: The spreading of individuals away from a centre, used in ecology and in studies of migration.
entries.definitionCN: 个体从中心向外散开，用于生态学与迁移研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real root and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、真实的词根与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means out: emigration is the view from the door being closed behind you.
normal.cn: 前缀意为向外：向外移民就是从身后那扇关上的门看到的情形。

normal.en: The pair emigration and immigration differ only in the direction of the prefix.
normal.cn: 向外移民与向内移民这一对词，只差前缀的方向。

normal.en: The person noun ends in a suffix marking the one who acts.
normal.cn: 指人的名词以一个标记施动者的词尾收束。

normal.en: Fixed phrases such as emigration policy and net emigration belong to the statistical sense.
normal.cn: 外迁政策、净迁出这类固定搭配属于统计义。

normal.en: In ecology the same word names the outgoing half of dispersal.
normal.cn: 在生态学中，同一个词命名扩散中出去的那一半。

abstract.en: Picture a door closing on a room that will keep the shape of your absence.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门关上，房间里将一直留着你的空缺形状。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with departures on one pan and arrivals on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一只盘放离开，另一只放到来。

abstract.en: Picture a map with an arrow pointing off its own edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，箭头指向地图边缘之外。

examples.en: Emigration rose when land prices collapsed in the countryside.
examples.cn: 乡村地价崩跌时，向外移民增加了。

examples.en: The government tried to slow emigration by offering rural loans.
examples.cn: 政府试图通过提供农村贷款来减缓向外移民。

examples.en: Emigration and immigration are recorded as separate lines in the census.
examples.cn: 在普查中，迁出与迁入被记为两条独立的项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一民·出去」——一批人离开本国到别处定居，就是向外移民

root: 拉丁 e- 或 ex-「向外」+ migrare「迁移」→ emigrare「迁出」；英语 emigration 于 17 世纪由 emigrate 的词干构成。migrare 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one departure: the act of leaving, the volume of leavers, the ledger entry, the founding of communities abroad, state policy, a historical wave, the outgoing half of biological dispersal and the flight of wealth to a lower-tax home.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次离开展开：离开的行为、离开者的总量、账簿上的一行、海外社群的形成、国家政策、历史浪潮、生物扩散中出去的一半，以及财富迁往低税地的迁徙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a suitcase on a quay, its old address label still stuck under the new one.
core.cn: 核心意象：码头上一只行李箱，旧地址标签仍压在新标签之下。

branches.en: LEAVING: the base act of departing in order to settle elsewhere.
branches.cn: 离开：为在别处定居而出走的基础行为。

branches.en: FLOW AND WAVE: counted departures become a measurable flow and then a historical wave.
branches.cn: 流量与浪潮：被计数的离开成为可测量的流量，再成为历史浪潮。

branches.en: LEDGER: emigration is a subtraction in the population account.
branches.cn: 账簿：迁出是人口账户中的一笔减法。

branches.en: ELSEWHERE: the same outflow builds communities abroad and, in finance, moves wealth between tax jurisdictions.
branches.cn: 别处：同一股流出在海外建起社群，在金融中则把财富移出税区。

branches.en: RULES AND NATURE: the state can restrict exits, and in ecology the word names dispersing individuals.
branches.cn: 规则与自然：国家可以限制出境，而在生态学中这个词指扩散的个体。

intro.en: Emigration is a prefix, a root and a suffix, and the family can be read from those pieces.
intro.cn: emigration 由一个前缀、一个词根与一个后缀构成，整个词族都可以按这些成分读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin e- marks motion outward, migrare supplies the root of moving, and -ation turns the verb into the name of the process.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 e- 标记向外移动，migrare 提供「迁移」的词根，-ation 把动词变成过程之名。

items.example: The prefix turns the movement away from home.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把移动转向离开家乡。

items.example: The root carries the idea of changing place.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着更换地点的意思。

items.meaning: to move out of a country
items.example: Her family emigrated in 1901.
items.exampleCN: 她的家庭在 1901 年迁出。

items.example: It builds the person noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成指人的名词。

items.example: The emigrant sold the last of the furniture.
items.exampleCN: 这位迁出者卖掉了最后一件家具。

items.example: It turns the verb into the name of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成过程之名。

items.example: Emigration emptied the coastal villages.
items.exampleCN: 向外移民使沿海村庄空了下来。

items.example: It forms the adjective of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示这一过程的形容词。

items.example: The emigratory flow lasted thirty years.
items.exampleCN: 向外移民的流动持续了三十年。

items.example: Migration can be internal or international.
items.exampleCN: 迁移可以是国内的，也可以是跨国的。

definition_zh: 移居国外者；迁出者；（作定语）迁出的
definition_en: a person who leaves their own country in order to settle in another
core_image: 一个人站在出境闸口，手里握着单程票，行李车上只剩一只箱子
scene: 出境闸口的玻璃门外，母亲挥手，年轻人把单程票塞进外套口袋。Every emigrant in the survey sent money home at least once a year.
sceneCN: 这里 emigrant 指「离开本国到他国定居的人」（第 1 个义项：向外迁移的人）；句意为调查中的每一位迁出者每年至少寄钱回家一次。图中可辨识物件：出境闸口、单程票、挥手的人、只剩一只箱子的行李车。

pos.zh: 移居国外者；迁出者（可数）
迁出的；向外移民的（作定语）

senses.title: A person who leaves to settle abroad
senses.titleCN: 离开本国到他国定居的人
senses.definition: someone who departs from their own country in order to make a home in another
senses.definitionCN: 离开本国并打算在他国安家的人
senses.example: Every emigrant in the survey sent money home at least once a year.
senses.exampleCN: 调查中的每一位迁出者每年至少寄钱回家一次。
senses.why: the word is the person noun of the verb of leaving, so it names the one who has made the outward crossing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「迁出」动词的人称名词，指完成那次向外越境的人。

senses.title: Used before a noun
senses.definition: used attributively for ships, families, workers or communities connected with leaving
senses.definitionCN: 作定语，用于与离开有关的船只、家庭、工人或社群
senses.example: Emigrant ships left the harbour every week in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 春天每周都有移民船离开港口。
senses.why: English lets a person noun modify another noun without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许人称名词不加变化地修饰另一个名词。

senses.title: A political exile
senses.definition: a person who leaves because of persecution or political pressure rather than free choice
senses.definitionCN: 因迫害或政治压力而非自由选择而离开的人
senses.example: The poet lived as an emigrant in three capitals.
senses.exampleCN: 这位诗人在三座首都以流亡者身份生活。
senses.why: the older word for a person who leaves has long covered those pushed out as well as those who choose to go.
senses.whyCN: 这个指离开者的旧词，长期以来既涵盖被逼走的人，也涵盖自愿离开的人。

senses.title: A contract labourer abroad
senses.definition: a worker who leaves to take a job in another country, often temporarily
senses.definitionCN: 离开本国到另一国工作的人，常为临时性
senses.example: Emigrant workers built the railway and then returned home.
senses.exampleCN: 外迁劳工修完铁路后回了家。
senses.why: labour demand turns the settler into a worker who may return, and the noun follows the person, not the intention.
senses.whyCN: 劳动力需求把定居者变成可能归来的工人，名词跟随的是人，而非意图。

senses.title: A person who returns
senses.definition: a former emigrant who comes back to the country of origin
senses.definitionCN: 回到原籍国的昔日迁出者
senses.example: Returning emigrants brought savings and new building styles.
senses.exampleCN: 归国的迁出者带回了积蓄与新的建筑样式。
senses.why: the label sticks to the person even after the move is reversed, which is why the returning form is needed.
senses.whyCN: 即使移动已经反向，这个标签仍跟着人，因此需要「归国的」这一说法。

senses.title: A community abroad
senses.definition: emigrants from one place considered together as a group in their new country
senses.definitionCN: 来自同一地方的迁出者在新国家作为整体来看
senses.example: The emigrant community funded a school in the old village.
senses.exampleCN: 海外侨民群体在老村资助了一所学校。
senses.why: a collection of individuals becomes a social body with its own institutions and money.
senses.whyCN: 个体的集合会变成拥有自身机构与资金的社会体。

senses.title: A dispersing organism
senses.definition: an individual that leaves a population to settle elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 离开原种群到他处立足的个体
senses.example: Each emigrant wolf must find unoccupied territory.
senses.exampleCN: 每一只迁出的狼都必须找到未被占据的领地。
senses.why: ecology borrows the human noun for the individual that leaves a group, matching the verb of departure.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用这个指人的名词，指离开群体的个体，与表离开的动词相配。

senses.title: A passenger-list category
senses.titleCN: 乘客名单上的登记类别
senses.definition: a person recorded under the heading of emigrants in shipping or border records
senses.definitionCN: 在航运或边境记录中以迁出者名目登记的人
senses.example: The archive lists him as an emigrant, though he later returned.
senses.exampleCN: 档案把他登记为迁出者，尽管他后来回来了。
senses.why: administrative records turn a moving person into a ticked box, and the box keeps its own name.
senses.whyCN: 行政记录把移动中的人变成一个勾选栏，而这个栏位保留了自己的名称。

intro.en: Emigrant is the present participle stem of Latin emigrare 'to move out', from e- 'out' plus migrare 'to migrate'. English took it from French in the eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: emigrant 是拉丁 emigrare「迁出」的现在分词词干，由 e-「向外」与 migrare「迁移」构成。英语在 18 世纪经法语吸收。年代均为约数。

items.en: Migrare meant 'to move, change one's dwelling'. Its earlier origin is not established, and the root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: migrare 意为「迁移、更换住所」。它更早的来源未得到证明，为其提出的词根属重构形式。

items.en: E- 'out' plus migrare gave emigrare 'to move out of a place'. Its participle emigrans named a person in the act of leaving.
items.cn: e-「向外」加 migrare 构成 emigrare「迁出某地」，其分词 emigrans 指正在离开的人。

items.en: French emigrant carried the participle into English as a noun, in the same period when immigration and emigration were settling into their modern pair.
items.cn: 法语 emigrant 把这个分词作为名词带入英语，正值迁入与迁出两个名词逐渐固定为现代配对之时。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the noun covered settlers, contract workers and political exiles alike.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，这个名词已同时涵盖定居者、合同劳工与政治流亡者。

items.en: Nineteenth-century passenger lists made the word a bureaucratic category, which is why the returning form later became necessary.
items.cn: 19 世纪的乘客名单使这个词成为官僚分类，这也是后来需要「归国的」这一说法的原因。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin history of migrare is unsettled, and the earliest English citation is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：migrare 在拉丁语之前的历史尚无定论，最早的英语书证也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the direction words that differ by a single prefix; group two holds other names for people living away from home.
note.cn: 第一组是只差一个前缀的方向词；第二组是对离家者的其他称呼。

entries.definition: The person at the receiving end of the same crossing; one individual is both an emigrant and an immigrant at once.
entries.definitionCN: 同一次越境在接收端的那个人；同一个人可以同时是迁出者与迁入者。

entries.definition: Anyone or anything that moves between places, with no prefix and no fixed direction; it also covers internal movement.
entries.definitionCN: 任何在各地之间移动的人或物，没有前缀也没有固定方向；也涵盖国内流动。

entries.definition: The act or flow of leaving, not a single person.
entries.definitionCN: 离开的行为或流量，不是单个人。

entries.definition: To move into a country; its prefix points at the destination rather than the origin.
entries.definitionCN: 移入某国；前缀指向目的地而非原籍。

entries.definition: A person living outside their own country, often for work; the word usually implies choice and a continuing link home.
entries.definitionCN: 居住在国外的人，常因工作；通常暗示自愿选择并保持与家乡的联系。

entries.definition: A person forced to live away from home, or the state of being so forced; compulsion is central.
entries.definitionCN: 被迫离家居住的人，或这种状态；强迫性是核心。

entries.definition: A person outside their country because of war or persecution, with a legal status that emigrant does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 因战争或迫害而身在他国的人，拥有迁出者一词所不包含的法律身份。

entries.definition: A person who takes up land and builds a permanent home, seen from the destination rather than the departure.
entries.definitionCN: 占据土地并建立永久居所的人，从目的地而非出发地来看。

normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、真实的词根与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means out: the emigrant is the one walking away from the gate.
normal.cn: 前缀意为向外：迁出者就是走出闸口的那个人。

normal.en: The pair emigrant and immigrant differ only in the direction of the prefix.
normal.cn: 迁出者与迁入者这一对词，只差前缀的方向。

normal.en: The person noun ends in a suffix marking the one who acts.
normal.cn: 指人的名词以一个标记施动者的词尾收束。

normal.en: Fixed phrases such as emigrant ship and emigrant community belong to the historical and social senses.
normal.cn: 移民船、海外侨民社群这类固定搭配属于历史与社会义。

normal.en: In ecology the same noun names an individual that leaves its pack.
normal.cn: 在生态学中，同一个名词指离开群体的个体。

abstract.en: Picture a single ticket that has no return half.
abstract.cn: 想象一张没有回程联的单程票。

abstract.en: Picture a family photograph left behind in a drawer on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被故意留在抽屉里的全家福。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow drawn from a house outward, with the house still visible at its tail.
abstract.cn: 想象一支从房屋画出的箭头，箭尾仍看得见那所房子。

examples.en: The emigrant sent a third of his wages to his parents every month.
examples.cn: 这位迁出者每月把三分之一的工资寄给父母。

examples.en: Emigrant associations raised money for schools back home.
examples.cn: 迁出者协会为家乡的学校筹款。

examples.en: The museum displays letters written by emigrants on the voyage.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出迁出者在航程中写的信件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一民·出去」——一个人离开本国去别处定居，就是迁出者

root: 拉丁 e-「向外」+ migrare「迁移」→ emigrare「迁出」，取其现在分词词干加人称词尾得 emigrant。migrare 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person at the gate: the one who leaves to settle abroad, a modifier before a noun, an exile, a contract worker, one who returns, a community abroad, a dispersing animal and a box ticked on a passenger list.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕闸口前的同一个人展开：离开并到国外定居的人、名词前的修饰语、流亡者、合同劳工、归国者、海外社群、扩散的动物，以及乘客名单上被勾选的一栏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller at the departure gate holding a one-way ticket.
core.cn: 核心意象：出境闸口前一名旅客握着单程票。

branches.en: THE LEAVER: the base sense, the person who departs in order to settle elsewhere.
branches.cn: 离开者：基础义，为在别处定居而出走的人。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the noun doubles as a modifier in fixed phrases.
branches.cn: 语法：这个名词在固定搭配中兼作修饰语。

branches.en: MOTIVE: persecution pushes some out, and work pulls others away.
branches.cn: 动机：迫害把一些人推走，工作把另一些人拉走。

branches.en: AFTERWARD: the label persists through a return, and a crowd of leavers becomes a community abroad.
branches.cn: 之后：标签在人归国后仍然跟着，而一群离开者会在海外成为社群。

branches.en: NATURE AND PAPER: an animal dispersing, and a name entered in a shipping ledger.
branches.cn: 自然与纸面：扩散的动物，以及写进航运登记簿的名字。

intro.en: Emigrant is a prefix, a root and a person suffix, and the same pieces build the migration family.
intro.cn: emigrant 由一个前缀、一个词根与一个表人后缀构成，同样的成分构成整个迁移词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin e- marks motion outward, migrare supplies the root of moving, and the participle ending -ant names the person doing it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 e- 标记向外移动，migrare 提供「迁移」的词根，分词词尾 -ant 为做这件事的人命名。

items.example: The prefix points away from the home country.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀指向远离故土的方向。

items.example: The root carries the idea of moving home.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着搬迁的意思。

items.meaning: to move out of a country
items.example: They emigrated after the factory closed.
items.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后他们迁出。

items.example: It builds the person noun from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词构成指人的名词。

items.example: The emigrant carried one suitcase.
items.exampleCN: 这位迁出者只带了一只箱子。

items.example: It names the process rather than the person.
items.exampleCN: 它命名过程而非人。

items.example: Emigration reduced the village to half its size.
items.exampleCN: 向外移民使这个村子只剩一半人口。

items.example: It forms the adjective of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示这一过程的形容词。

items.example: The emigratory route ran through the port.
items.exampleCN: 向外移民的路线经过这个港口。

items.example: Migration may be seasonal or permanent.
items.exampleCN: 迁移可以是季节性的，也可以是永久的。

definition_zh: 人口转变；人口过渡（人口从高出生、高死亡转向低出生、低死亡的历史过程）
definition_en: the historical shift of a population from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates
core_image: 两列并排的曲线，先是一条高死亡线缓缓下降，随后生育线跟着下降，最后两条线在低处并行
scene: 村口诊所的墙上挂着两张旧图，一张记婴儿夭折，一张记每户孩子数目。The demographic transition began when death rates fell ahead of birth rates.
sceneCN: 这里 demographic transition 指「人口从高出生高死亡转向低出生低死亡的过程」（第 1 个义项：整体转变过程）；句意为人口转变始于死亡率先于出生率下降。图中可辨识物件：两张旧图、下降的死亡曲线、稍后下降的生育曲线、低处并行的双线。

pos.zh: 人口转变；人口过渡（可数，指一次转变）

collocations.phrase: a stage of the demographic transition

senses.title: The whole historical shift
senses.definition: the long change by which a population moves from high birth and death rates to low ones
senses.definitionCN: 人口从高出生率、高死亡率走向低出生率、低死亡率的长期变化
senses.example: The demographic transition began when death rates fell ahead of birth rates.
senses.exampleCN: 人口转变始于死亡率先于出生率下降。
senses.why: transition means going across from one state to another, so the phrase names a crossing between two demographic regimes.
senses.whyCN: transition 意为从一种状态跨到另一种，因此这个短语命名的是两种人口状态之间的跨越。

senses.title: Stage one: high births, high deaths
senses.titleCN: 第一阶段：高出生、高死亡
senses.definition: the pre-industrial balance in which both birth and death rates are high and growth is slow
senses.definitionCN: 工业化之前的平衡状态，出生与死亡都高，增长缓慢
senses.example: In stage one, families were large but few children reached adulthood.
senses.exampleCN: 在第一阶段，家庭规模大，但很少孩子能活到成年。
senses.why: the model begins with the regime that existed before medicine, sanitation and machine farming.
senses.whyCN: 模型从医学、卫生与机械农业出现之前的那种状态开始。

senses.title: Stage two: deaths fall first
senses.definition: the phase in which mortality drops while fertility stays high, producing rapid growth
senses.definitionCN: 死亡率下降而生育率仍高的阶段，人口因而快速增长
senses.example: Stage two brought a population boom as deaths fell but births did not.
senses.exampleCN: 第二阶段死亡下降而出生未降，带来了人口激增。
senses.why: the gap between falling deaths and unchanged births is what makes the transition visible as a spike.
senses.whyCN: 死亡下降与出生不变之间的缺口，使这次转变在曲线上表现为一个尖峰。

senses.title: Stage three: births follow down
senses.titleCN: 第三阶段：出生率随后下降
senses.definition: the phase in which fertility begins to fall and growth slows
senses.definitionCN: 生育率开始下降、增长速度放缓的阶段
senses.example: Schools closed in stage three as each family had fewer children.
senses.exampleCN: 进入第三阶段后，家庭孩子减少，学校随之关停。
senses.why: once survival is assured, parents begin to choose family size, and the birth line follows the death line down.
senses.whyCN: 一旦存活有保障，父母开始选择家庭规模，出生线便跟着死亡线一起下降。

senses.title: Stage four: low and stable
senses.definition: the end state in which both rates are low and the population is roughly stable
senses.definitionCN: 终态，出生与死亡都低，人口大致稳定
senses.example: The country reached stage four after a century of falling fertility.
senses.exampleCN: 经过一个世纪生育率下降，这个国家进入了第四阶段。
senses.why: low death rates and small families balance each other, so the curve flattens.
senses.whyCN: 低死亡与小家庭相互平衡，曲线因此变平。

senses.title: Stage five: below replacement
senses.titleCN: 第五阶段：低于更替水平
senses.definition: a late phase in which births fall below deaths and the population begins to shrink
senses.definitionCN: 晚期阶段，出生低于死亡，人口开始缩减
senses.example: Some models add a fifth stage of sustained shrinking.
senses.exampleCN: 一些模型加上了持续缩减的第五阶段。
senses.why: the original model stopped at stability, but several countries went past that point, so a fifth stage was added.
senses.whyCN: 原模型止于稳定，但若干国家越过了那一点，因此补出了第五阶段。

senses.title: The model as an analytic tool
senses.titleCN: 作为分析工具的人口转变模型
senses.definition: the staged diagram used to compare countries and to predict population growth
senses.definitionCN: 用来比较各国并预测人口增长的分阶段图示
senses.example: Teachers use the demographic transition to explain two centuries of growth.
senses.exampleCN: 教师用人口转变来解释两个世纪的增长。
senses.why: a process becomes a model when its stages are drawn as a standard diagram that can be taught and compared.
senses.whyCN: 当各个阶段被画成可教学、可比较的标准图示时，过程就成了模型。

senses.title: Critiques and later variants
senses.definition: the revision of the model for societies whose fertility fell for reasons of values and gender rather than income alone
senses.definitionCN: 针对生育下降源于价值观与性别而非仅收入的社会，对模型作出的修正
senses.example: The second demographic transition points to changing family values, not just rising income.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次人口转变把注意力放在家庭观念的变化，而不只是收入上升。
senses.why: the model was drawn from European history, so later scholars added variants for societies that did not follow the same path.
senses.whyCN: 模型取自欧洲历史，后来的学者便为路径不同的社会补出变体。

intro.en: Demographic joins Greek demos 'people' with -graphia 'writing, description'; transition comes from Latin transire 'to go across'. The phrase is a twentieth-century term in demography. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: demographic 由希腊 dēmos「民众」与 -graphia「书写、描述」构成；transition 来自拉丁 transire「越过」。这个短语是 20 世纪人口学的术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Demos meant 'the people, the common folk'. It also gives democracy; its deeper origin is not settled.
items.cn: dēmos 意为「民众、普通人」，也构成 democracy 的前半；其更深来源尚无定论。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to scratch, write', and -graphia named a written description or a field of study.
items.cn: graphein 意为「刻写、书写」，-graphia 指书面描述或一门研究。

items.en: Transire 'to go across' is trans- 'across' plus ire 'to go'; transition is its noun of action.
items.cn: transire「越过」由 trans-「跨越」与 ire「走」构成；transition 是它的动作名词。

items.en: Demography was coined in the nineteenth century for the statistical study of populations, and transition entered social science through Latin.
items.cn: 人口学一词在 19 世纪为人口的统计研究而造，转变一词则经拉丁语进入社会科学。

items.en: The fixed phrase spread in mid-twentieth-century demography, when long census series made the fall of death and birth rates visible as stages.
items.cn: 这个固定短语在 20 世纪中期的人口学中扩散，当时长时段的普查序列使死亡与出生的下降显现为阶段。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origins): the earliest use of the exact phrase is not precisely recorded, and the pre-Greek origin of demos is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这一确切短语的最早使用没有精确记录；dēmos 在希腊语之前的来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds demographic terms that share the adjective but name different things; group two holds related transitions and outcomes.
note.cn: 第一组是共享同一形容词但所指不同的人口学术语；第二组是相关的转变与结果。

entries.definition: The staged graph itself, a teaching and forecasting tool rather than the historical process it describes.
entries.definitionCN: 那张分阶段图示本身，是教学与预测工具，而非它所描述的历史过程。

entries.definition: The growth that follows when a large share of the population is of working age; a consequence, not the transition.
entries.definitionCN: 当劳动年龄人口占比很大时带来的增长；是转变的结果，而非转变本身。

entries.definition: The shift from infectious to chronic disease as the main cause of death; it runs alongside the demographic one but is not identical.
entries.definitionCN: 主要死因从传染病转向慢性病；与人口转变并行，但并非同一件事。

entries.definition: Falling numbers, which can follow the transition's later stages but is not the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 人口数量下降，可能是转变后期的结果，但不是转变过程本身。

entries.definition: The fall in birth rates alone; it is the second half of the demographic transition.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指出生率的下降，是人口转变的后半段。

entries.definition: The fall in death rates alone, which usually comes first and triggers the growth spike.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指死亡率的下降，通常先发生并引发增长尖峰。

entries.definition: The broader turn toward industry, schooling and urban life of which demographic change is one strand.
entries.definitionCN: 朝向工业、教育与城市生活的更广泛转变，人口变化只是其中一条线索。

entries.definition: The later fall of fertility driven by changing values and gender roles, added as a revision of the classic model.
entries.definitionCN: 由价值观与性别角色变化驱动的后期生育下降，作为对经典模型的修正而加入。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Demographic means of the people, and transition means crossing, so the phrase is a people-crossing from one regime to another.
normal.cn: 人口的一词意为属于民众，转变一词意为跨越，因此这个短语就是民众从一种状态跨到另一种。

normal.en: The model always runs deaths down first, births second.
normal.cn: 这个模型总是先让死亡下降，再让出生下降。

normal.en: Stage one is high and high; stage four is low and low.
normal.cn: 第一阶段是高与高，第四阶段是低与低。

normal.en: Fixed phrases such as demographic transition model and second demographic transition mark the teaching and revision senses.
normal.cn: 人口转变模型、第二次人口转变这类固定搭配标出教学与修正两个义项。

normal.en: The word demographic also appears in demographic dividend and demographic decline.
normal.cn: 人口的这一形容词还出现在人口红利与人口下降等说法中。

abstract.en: Picture two lines walking downstairs, the death line first and the birth line a few steps behind.
abstract.cn: 想象两条线一起下楼，死亡线先走，出生线落后几步。

abstract.en: Picture a see-saw that stays level only when both children are the same weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一架跷跷板，只有两边孩子体重相同时才保持水平。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked stage one on one side and stage four on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，两面分别写着第一阶段与第四阶段。

examples.en: Most high-income countries completed the demographic transition before 1980.
examples.cn: 多数高收入国家在 1980 年前完成了人口转变。

examples.en: The demographic transition in that region was compressed into three decades.
examples.cn: 该地区的人口转变被压缩在三十年内完成。

examples.en: Migration can delay the final stage of the demographic transition.
examples.cn: 迁移可以推迟人口转变的最后阶段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「人口（demographic）+ 过渡（transition）」——人口从高生高死走向低生低死的过渡

root: 希腊 dēmos「民众」+ graphein「书写」构成 demographic；拉丁 trans-「跨越」+ ire「走」构成 transition。两词在 20 世纪人口学中固定连用。dēmos 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one long crossing: the whole shift, each of its four or five stages, the diagram that teaches it, and the revisions made when some societies took a different path.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次漫长的跨越展开：整体转变、它的四到五个阶段、用来讲授它的图示，以及当一些社会走上不同道路时所作的修正。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two curves descending at different times and then running level at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条在不同时间下降、最后在底部并行的曲线。

branches.en: START: the old regime of high births and high deaths, and the overall crossing away from it.
branches.cn: 起点：高出生高死亡的旧状态，以及离开它的整体跨越。

branches.en: THE GAP: deaths drop first, and the widening gap is population growth.
branches.cn: 缺口：死亡先降，不断扩大的缺口就是人口增长。

branches.en: CLOSING: births follow down until both lines run low and level.
branches.cn: 收拢：出生随后下降，直到两条线都在低处走平。

branches.en: OVERSHOOT: some populations go past replacement and begin to shrink.
branches.cn: 越界：一些人口越过更替水平，开始缩减。

branches.en: THE TOOL AND ITS REVISIONS: the staged diagram, plus the variants written for societies that diverged.
branches.cn: 工具与修正：分阶段图示，以及为走上不同道路的社会所写的变体。

intro.en: The phrase is built from Greek and Latin pieces that also build the vocabulary of population studies.
intro.cn: 这个短语由希腊与拉丁成分构成，这些成分也构成人口研究的大部分词汇。

latinIntro.en: Greek demos and graphein build demography; Latin trans- and ire build transition, and the two word families meet in this phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 dēmos 与 graphein 构成人口学；拉丁 trans- 与 ire 构成转变，两个词族在这个短语中相遇。

items.example: The root names the population itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指人口本身。

items.example: It turns the root into the name of a study.
items.exampleCN: 它把词根变成一门研究之名。

items.meaningCN: 人口学；人口的统计研究
items.example: Demography counts births, deaths and moves.
items.exampleCN: 人口学统计出生、死亡与迁移。

items.example: A demographic survey asks about age and household.
items.exampleCN: 人口调查询问年龄与家庭情况。

items.example: The prefix marks a movement from one state to another.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记从一种状态到另一种的移动。
